title: harden-sse-framing-by-introducing-checkpoint-anchors-and-event-stabilizer
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We have recurring customer reports and internal canaries showing partial JSON emissions and out-of-order tool/function-call sentinels when network jitter causes SSE fragments to split mid-token or mid-UTF8 codepoint. This causes downstream OpenAI-compatible clients to surface parse errors and to occasionally drop function-call boundaries. This PR introduces a checkpoint-anchor protocol and an event stabilizer layer in the SSE emitter/adapter to make streaming resilient to fragment loss, late arrival, and split UTF-8 frames. Solution summary: 1) Checkpoint anchors: embed lightweight monotonic checkpoint tokens (anchor_id + seq_id) at soft boundaries in the stream; anchors are idempotent and can be retransmitted. 2) Heartbeat-aware repair: the emitter will create a checkpoint at heartbeat intervals and expose a resume token to the client so late fragments can be reconciled by replaying from the last anchor. 3) UTF-8 sentinel rewrite: ensure byte-level framing avoids splitting multi-byte UTF-8 sequences by rewriting split-byte placeholders into safe escape markers; the reassembler rewrites back on the receiving side. 4) JSON span fence: add a small state-machine that detects unterminated top-level JSON spans and delays terminal delimiter emission until a stable fence is reached (reduces partial JSON emission). 5) Backwards-compatible adapter: openai-compat adapter will emit anchor headers as optional SSE events ("anchor") and understands resume requests; flag ENABLE_SSE_CHECKPOINTS controls rollout. Implementation details: - New components: api/streaming/sse/checkpoint.{h,cpp} implements anchor generation and lease semantics; api/streaming/sse/parser.cpp extended with ReassemblyWindow and Utf8Sentinel state; openai-compat/streaming_adapter.go extended to accept resume headers and to emit anchor events; tests added in test/streaming/sse/test_partial_json_recovery.py and bench/streaming/reassembly-bench.yml. - The anchor token is a compact base62 string: anchor=<anchor_id>:<seq_id> and is emitted as an SSE event with type "anchor"; payload is minimal. - Resume semantics: client can send X-Resume-Anchor header with the last-seen anchor string; server will fast-forward reassembly from that anchor and avoid re-emitting completed spans. - Canary rollout: feature flag off by default; enable on 10% of hostnames for 48h, monitor metrics, then ramp to 100%. Metrics added: sse.anchor.emit, sse.anchor.misses, sse.reassembly.rescue, sse.utf8.sentinel_rewrites. Testing and validation: - Unit tests covering anchor generation, anchor id collisions, and UTF-8 boundary rewrite. - Integration tests that replay synthetic fragment reorderings and truncated chunk streams to exercise resume behavior. - End-to-end canary on staging with real traffic load reproducer. - Benchmarks show <1% median token latency increase under steady load, and 20-60% reduction in partial-JSON parse errors on simulated jitter. Rollback plan: if errors increase by >5% or latency SLOs breach, the flag will be turned off and a rollback automated workflow will revert the feature branch. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-9876) - [x] unit + integration tests added - [x] canary flag and rollout plan - [x] metrics and dashboards - [x] docs updated (docs/compat/sse-framing.md) Related: this complements earlier reassembly heuristics but focuses on a low-overhead resume path and UTF-8-safe framing, reducing the need for aggressive buffering.

review_comments: Luca Romano: Overall looks solid. Two things: ensure anchor emission is non-blocking and doesn't add tail latency; add a metric for anchors emitted per session.
Priya Nair: Addressed — anchor emission is now buffered and emitted asynchronously; added sse.anchor.emit metric and guard to back-pressure when queue grows.
Evan Hsu: Can we avoid changing semantics for clients that don't opt into resume header? Make sure no extra events break strict parsers.
Priya Nair: The adapter emits anchor events only when ENABLE_SSE_CHECKPOINTS=on; anchors are optional SSE events and documented as safe to ignore. Compatibility tests added.
Anika Sharma: Unit tests pass locally; CI had a flaky test in integration that I re-ran — looks good now.
CI Bot: Integration suite failed (test_stream_reassembly) on first run due to timing; re-run succeeded.
release_notes: - Improve SSE streaming resilience: checkpoint anchors + resume headers; optional UTF-8 sentinel handling; reduces partial JSON parse errors; opt-in via ENABLE_SSE_CHECKPOINTS feature flag.
notes_for_ops: Enable flag on 10% of hostnames for 48h, watch sse.reassembly.rescue and sse.anchor.misses; if sse.anchor.misses > 0.5% for 2h or tail latency P99 increases >10% rollback immediately.
rollback_instructions: Flag toggle off + automated revert workflow: /workflows/revert-sse-checkpoint on repo. Notify #sre and #platform if rollback triggered.
compatibility_notes: OpenAI-compat adapter emits optional anchor SSE events. Clients that ignore unknown SSE event types are unaffected. Resume header is optional; server will fall back to legacy reassembly if not provided.
